title: Sanitize tenant attribution for interleaved batched replays after key swap
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: A shard of customer requests that were queued during an API key swap can be replayed from the request buffer out-of-order and get attributed to the wrong project/org. This ticket investigates and implements a sanitizer that enforces deterministic tenant mapping for batched/replayed requests so attribution remains correct after key rotations and proxy handoffs.

Background: We observed two customer complaints where usage spikes appeared on unrelated projects immediately after a key rotation window. Early forensics show that an edge node had buffered ~300 small requests, received an API key swap signal, rewrote the request envelope, and then replayed the buffer while a background batch join loop continued to merge incoming traffic. The result: some buffered requests were processed with the new key binding and some with stale mapping; downstream metering aggregated both under the wrong project due to a race in the attribution hydration flow.

Scope: Covers runtime request ingress (proxy/batcher), attribution hydration service (tenant-resolver), and the metering ingestion pipeline that writes usage events. Does NOT include billing UI updates or downstream billing reconciliation automation (separate follow-up).
reproduction_steps: 1) Create two projects A and B in the same org and generate a long-lived API key template used by a proxy.
2) Start a steady stream of small generation requests (1-10 tokens) through the proxy at ~50rps.
3) Trigger a key swap event and simulate edge buffering by introducing a 1s stall on the proxy write path.
4) Allow buffered requests to replay concurrently with new requests; observe attribution tags and metering events in the warehouse.
Expected: All requests should be attributed to the project bound when the request was accepted (persisted mapping) so no cross-project bleed occurs.
investigation_notes: Observed that the proxy uses a soft-binding table that can be updated mid-batch; when replay runs it re-looks-up mapping which may return the new binding.
Batch join window allows mixing buffered items and live requests; the ordering of hydrate->enrich->emit is non-atomic across the batch boundary.
Tenant-resolver caches are TTLed aggressively (100ms) which makes mapping unstable during a rotation 'storm'.
Metering ingestion expects a stable 'attribution_id' in the event payload; when provenance changes mid-flight we see duplicate events with different attribution tags for the same logical request.
root_cause: Race between proxy buffer replay and tenant binding propagation: buffered requests are re-hydrated after key swap using the latest mapping rather than the mapping recorded at acceptance time. The batch-flush path does not pin attribution metadata atomically with the request body when buffering occurs.
proposed_solution: 1) Record and persist a compact attribution token (attribution_v1) upon request acceptance and store it alongside the buffered payload. 2) During replay, prefer the stored attribution token and skip a fresh tenant lookup. 3) Add a fast path sanitization step in the batch joiner that verifies attribution consistency for each batched item and rejects/rewrites items that are inconsistent. 4) Instrument metrics (replay-attributed-count, attribution-overrides) and add DAG tests. 5) Deploy as a staged rollout: canary on internal org, then opt-in customers, then global.
implementation_tasks: Proxy: append 'adhoc_attribution_token' to buffered envelope and persist with buffer shards (ENG work).
Tenant-resolver: expose deterministic attachment function and stable hashing for the token format.
Batcher: add sanitization step that pins attribution before emit and records override metric; fail fast for mismatches to avoid silent bleed.
Metering pipeline: accept attribution token and prefer it over request-scoped lookup; add reconciliation job to dedupe conflicting events for last 7 days.
End-to-end tests: unit tests for token encoding, integration test that simulates key swap and replay ordering, and load test at 200rps for 10 minutes.
acceptance_criteria: Automated integration test that reproduces previous leak scenario passes in CI and asserts zero cross-project events.
Canary rollout on staging org shows no attribution drift and metrics 'attribution-overrides' remain near 0 except during controlled tests.
No increase in tail latency (> p99) for batcher path beyond 10% under normal load after changes.
Reconciliation job able to identify and correct historical misattributed events for affected customers within SLA window.
testing_plan: Unit: token encode/decode fuzz tests, deterministic hashing tests.
Integration: end-to-end simulation with proxy stalling + key-swap orchestrator (uses internal test harness).
Load: 200rps steady + 2s replay burst to verify batching sanitization at scale.
Post-deploy: monitor 'replay-attributed-count' and 'attribution-override-rate' rolling 5m windows; set alert if override_rate > 0.05%.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature gate behind 'sanitize_replay_attribution' toggled off by default.
2) Deploy to canary cluster (internal) for 48 hours. Validate metrics and run synthetic harness.
3) Enable for 5 pilot customers (opt-in) and monitor for 72 hours.
4) Global release with monitoring and a 24-hour rollback window.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Breaking existing proxies that rely on current lookup behavior. Mitigation: feature-gate and backward-compatible token absent path.
Risk: Slight increase in buffer envelope size leading to higher memory usage. Mitigation: compact token (8 bytes) and shard-level eviction tuning.
Risk: Reconciliation may double-bill if not deduped. Mitigation: reconciliation job writes correction events and flags, does not trigger billing until verified.
